messages.content: 'Calculate the energy required to heat 100 grams of water from 25 degrees Celsius to 100 degrees Celsius in joules, and also calculate the energy required to heat the same mass of Aluminium under same conditions in joules

function.name: temperature_converter_convert

function.name: energy_calculator_calculate
function.description: Calculate the energy needed to heat a substance from an initial to a final temperature. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in grams. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degrees Celsius. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit to report the energy in. Options are 'joules' and 'calories'. Defaults to 'joules'.

message.content:
**Energy needed to raise the temperature**

The amount of sensible heat \(Q\) required to change the temperature of a material is given by  

\[
Q \;=\; m\,c_p\,\Delta T
\]

where  
\(m\) – mass of the sample (grams),  
\(c_p\) – specific‑heat capacity (J / (g ⋅ °C)),  
\(\Delta T\) – temperature rise (°C).

| Substance | Typical \(c_p\) (J / (g ⋅ °C)) |
|-----------|------------------------------|
| Water     | **4.186**                    |
| Aluminum  | **0.900** (≈ 0.897–0.901 depending on range) |

---

### 1. Heating 100 g of water from 25 °C → 100 °C

\[
\begin{aligned}
m &= 100~{\rm g}\\[4pt]
\Delta T &= 100^\circ C - 25^\circ C = 75^\circ C\\[4pt]
Q_{\text{H₂O}} &= 100~{\rm g}\;\times\;4.186~{\rm J/(g\,^{\circ}{\rm C})}\;\times\;75~^{\circ}{\rm C}\\
&= 31,\!395~{\rm J}\\
&\approx {\bf 3.14\times10^4~J}\;(31.4~{\rm kJ})
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** ≈ 31 400 J (or 31.4 kJ)

---

### 2. Heating 100 g of aluminum from 25 °C → 100 °C

\[
\begin{aligned}
m &= 100~{\rm g}\\[4pt]
\Delta T &= 75^\circ C\\[4pt]
Q_{\text{Al}} &= 100~{\rm g}\;\times\;0.900~{\rm J/(g\,^{\circ}{\rm C})}\;\times\;75~^{\circ}{\rm C}\\
&= 6,\!750~{\rm J}\\
&\approx {\bf 6.75\times10^3~J}\;(6.75~{\rm kJ})
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** ≈ 6 800 J (or 6.8 kJ)

---

#### Summary table

| Material   | Heat required (J) | Heat required (kJ) |
|------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| Water      | 31 395            | 31.4               |
| Aluminum   | 6 750             | 6.75              |

These calculations assume constant specific‑heat capacities over the 25 → 100 °C interval and neglect phase changes or other effects such as pressure variations.
